summary: The “Monitoring Guidelines” are intended to be a companion document to the “ Supervision Guidelines ”. The goal of the “Monitoring Guidelines” is to provide general recommendations for graduate units on creating structures and processes to support doctoral student success by ensuring that students can make timely progression through their programs. There is likely to be considerable variance in the implementation of some of the recommended procedures, depending, for example, on the nature of the scholarly discipline and the research environment (including the size of graduate unit), or the degree to which research is conducted independently. Graduate units are encouraged to implement the guidelines in a manner appropriate to their discipline and program as well as communicate the relevant procedures in a clear and transparent manner to graduate students and faculty.

What follows are the procedures for the award of a PhD degree, and those for Master’s degrees.
requirements: PhD requirement: Appraisal of the thesis from the supervisor or another supervisory committee member, plus a positive appraisal from an external appraiser with an arm's length relationship.
PhD requirement: Recommendation by the graduate unit to accept the thesis as fulfilling PhD degree requirements.
Master's requirement: Submission including program transcript confirming completion percentage.
Master's requirement: Where only a final examination or terminal requirement remains outstanding, an aegrotat grade may be assigned.
Master's requirement: Where a thesis is required, graduate units may reach out to SGS for guidance.
Approval required from both the Non-Standard Admissions and Programs Committee and the Academic Board of Governing Council.
documents: Letter from the Chair or Graduate Coordinator of the relevant graduate unit submitted to SGS (addressed to the Associate Director, Graduate Academic Services) outlining circumstances and recommendation.
Consent from the student's family or estate provided to the graduate unit.
Appraisal of PhD thesis from the supervisor or supervisory committee member.
Appraisal of PhD thesis from an external appraiser.
Certification of arm's length relationship between external appraiser, supervisor, and candidate.
Program transcript confirming completion percentage (for Master's degree recommendations).
benefits: Posthumous conferral of a PhD or Master's degree.
Formal letter from the Dean, School of Graduate Studies, to the family reporting the positive decision.
eligibility: The deceased student must have been registered in good standing at the time of death or within the preceding 12 months.
The student's family or estate must consent to the posthumous conferral of the degree.
For PhD candidates: Must have a body of work constituting a thesis that could be submitted for publication, mostly the work of the candidate, which the graduate unit recommends accepting.
For Master's candidates: Must have completed at least 75% of total program credit requirements at the time of death.
howToApply: The Chair or Graduate Coordinator of the student's graduate unit submits a recommendation letter and supporting documents to the SGS Associate Director, Graduate Academic Services.
For PhD candidates, the graduate unit obtains internal appraisals and certifies the external appraiser's arm's length status; the Dean or designate appoints the external appraiser.
If appraisals and conditions are met, the graduate unit forwards the recommendation to the Non-Standard Admissions and Programs Committee.
Upon approval by the Non-Standard Admissions and Programs Committee, the recommendation is submitted to the Academic Board of Governing Council.
If approved by the Academic Board, SGS informs the graduate unit, and the Dean of SGS writes a letter to the student's family.
selectionProcess: Review and recommendation by the relevant graduate unit Chair or Graduate Coordinator.
Internal and external appraisal of the thesis (for PhD candidates).
Review and approval by the Non-Standard Admissions and Programs Committee.
Final approval by the Academic Board of Governing Council.
requiresSupervisor: The thesis supervisor or another supervisory committee member must provide an appraisal of the PhD thesis. The supervisor may perform some editorial work on the thesis, but the work must be mostly the candidate's.
